current.text: He is likely Minnesota's sixth man, a bench scorer projected for about 29 to 30 minutes.
He may close games in small lineups instead of Jonathan Kuminga, and he may play more minutes than Josh Green.
Minnesota's fifth starting spot is open. Kuminga and Josh Green are the other options for it.
LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards are Minnesota's lead guards, so he shares the ball with them.
Even if he starts, he is at best the third offensive option. His usage will probably drop, which caps his fantasy upside.
Last season his 3P% rose from 33 to 44 and his FT% rose from about 78 to 88.
Experts do not trust his shooting jump and expect it to come back down. His 71% deflection-to-steal conversion is also likely to regress.
If his shooting falls back to 49% from the field and 79% from the line, he is roughly a 140 to 180 player.
He is overvalued at his rank of 108 (round 9) and a fade at that price. He is fine as a late pick.
He is a tier 8 point guard, and tier 7 in points leagues.
With a March 28 season end, Minnesota plays 4, 2 and 4 games in our playoff weeks. The two-game week starts March 15 and is the semifinal.
Minnesota has 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Minnesota plays small, guard-heavy lineups. Its bench unit has no ball handlers and there is little scoring punch off the bench.
Minnesota should be competitive. One expert predicts 53 wins, so the team will not rest players to tank.

note: Both sites rank him 108 and average costs are only 1.1 USD (values 4 and 2 USD), so he is a last-dollar guard in our 144-player draft and not worth a bid war. His projected 50% FG and 86% FT on about 15 points help any build. But that line rests on a shooting jump the experts expect to fade, and if it does he drops to about 140 to 180, outside our draft pool. Early in the season, check whether he starts or comes off the bench, whether he closes games ahead of Kuminga, and whether his FT% and 3P% hold. Also remember Minnesota's two-game semifinal week.
